entries.text: Bitcoin is a decentralized digital currency. Unlike traditional money, it doesn't rely on a central bank.
It uses a public ledger called a blockchain. Every transaction is grouped into a block, linked to the previous one, creating an immutable chain.
To secure the network, miners compete to solve complex mathematical puzzles. This process, called Proof of Work, prevents fraud and issues new coins.
Your identity is protected by cryptography. A public key acts as your address, while a private key is the secret password that allows you to spend your funds.
By removing the middleman, Bitcoin creates a peer-to-peer system for value. That's how Bitcoin works.
